# dsh-beads-viewer

**Beads issues in the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar** — the browser counterpart of
the terminal `bv

ssues in the DeepSeek Harness right sidebar** — the browser counterpart of
the terminal `bv` viewer.
🌏 **English** · 中文
| 浅色 Light | 深色 Dark |
## ✨ Features
| **🗂️ A tab beside Files** — registers a `beads` tab type in the sidebar's new-tab guide, dockable,
split and floatable like any other page. State survives a tab switch. | **🎨 Colour-coded badges** —
status, priority and type on every row, each dimension its own shape and hue. Label ink is derived
from each fill's luminance, so text is always legible; two fills can never read as the same colour (

ΔE ≥ 25, test-enforced). |
| **📏 Uniform rows** — exactly three line boxes tall (`calc(3 * 1lh + pad
ding)`), so the list scans as a grid. Long titles truncate at the container edge; the label track is
reserved even when empty. | **🖱️ Hover marks the target** — a resting row is plain; the row under t
he pointer takes a teal wash. One hue mixed against `transparent` reads correctly on both themes. |
| **🔍 Ready vs waiting** — a *Ready* chip from `bd ready`, a *Waiting* chip for issues held by open
blockers, plus the status chips with live counts, a search box (`/` focuses it) and sorting. | **📝 P
olished Markdown** — headings, nested and task lists, tables, fenced code, quotes and emphasis, rend

ered by a small built-in renderer. Long threads open on the newest comments. |
| **🔗 Clickable refer
ences** — a path that names a real project file opens in the document preview; an issue id opens tha
t issue. Both stay plain text when the target does not exist. | **🧾 Id at hand** — `⧉` copies it, `↵

` inserts it into the composer at the caret as one undoable edit. |
| **🌓 Theme in three ways** — th
e Host's text size, font choices and interface language (`zh` / `en`) all apply. | **🧩 Secondary blo
cks on a wash** — design, notes, acceptance criteria and comments sit on a faint accent wash; the de
scription stays primary. |

## 🚀 Installation
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then **restart the Harness** so the new bundle's client half loads (a hard browser
refresh also pick

s up a newer bundle). The tab appears in the right sidebar's
new-tab guide.

A **linked** install picks up edits on the next load with no reinstall; a registry
install is a norm
al package, so upgrading means running `add` again.
Requirements

- **The `bd` CLI** on the machine running the Harness. The Host finds it on `PATH`,
then at the usua

l Homebrew and Go install locations; `brew install beads` is
enough.
- **A project with a Beads work

space.** The panel asks `bd where` which workspace it
would open, so a subdirectory, a git worktree

and a `BEADS_DIR` override all
resolve the way `bd` itself would.

If either is missing the panel says which one — in the panel itself, with the reason
`bd` gave.
FAQ
| Symptom | Cause & fix |
| **Tab shows HTTP 404, but the search bar and filters are there** | The client half is a static ass
et and still rendered, but the data route was never registered — the plugin activated before the Hos
t's web server. Fixed in 1.0.0 by waiting on the service; if you see it on an older version, restart

the Harness. |
| **Fonts or sizes in the panel do not follow the Host's appearance settings** | Sam
e cause as above: the running client bundle is older than the page. Hard-refresh (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R).
The panel derives its sizes from `--dsh-content-font-size` and its fonts from the Host font variabl

es. |
| **`bd` not found** | Install it (`brew install beads`) or make sure it is on the `PATH` of t

he process running DSH. |
| **"This project has no Beads workspace"** | Run `bd init` in the project

, or point `BEADS_DIR` at an existing one. The panel shows the reason `bd` gave. |
| **A workspace t
hat used to open now reports a migration** | Old Beads workspaces must be migrated by `bd` itself; t

he panel prints `bd`'s instruction verbatim instead of guessing. |
| **Numbers in an ordered list lo
ok wider than the bullet beside them** | That is the point: the numbered gutter is wider (`2.35em` v
s `1.9em`) because digits need the room. The two lists share one text start. |
## 🔧 How it reads the tracker
The Host half serves one read-only route, `GET /beads-viewer/api`:
| Query | Answer |
| `?cwd=<dir>` | every issue (slim rows), status counts, the status vocabulary, and each issue's rea

diness |
| `?cwd=<dir>&action=issue&id=<id>` | the whole issue, its comments, and both dependency di

rections |
| `?cwd=<dir>&action=files&paths=<newline-separated>` | which of those paths exist, and w

ns |
| `?cwd=<dir>&action=files&paths=<newline-separated>` | which of those paths exist, and where |
`?force=1` bypasses the four-second list cache. Three properties are deliberate:

- **It shells out to `bd`, and reads no database file.** A Beads workspace is either
a Dolt server o

r a SQLite file depending on how it was initialised, and the schema
moves between `bd` releases. `bd

--json` is the interface that stays correct across
both — and when a workspace is too old, `bd` pri

nts the migration instruction,
which the panel shows verbatim rather than guessing at.
- **It is rea

d-only.** Every read goes through one `readBd` helper that prepends
`bd --readonly`, so the guarante

e is structural rather than a per-call habit — a
test asserts the flag is on the argv. No route muta

tes anything.
- **It only answers itself.** The route refuses non-loopback peers, and `?cwd=` must
b

e an existing directory that (or whose parent) holds `.beads`. The directory is
then used as the wor

kspace for every `bd` call, so a request cannot point `bd` at
an arbitrary tree.
